https://www.barrons.com/articles/apple-and-buffett-bring-a-floor-to-the-stock-says-bernstein-1525814037 Apple and Buffett Shore Up the Stock, Says Bernstein By May 8, 2018 5:13 p.m. ET Text Size Tiernan Ray May 8, 2018 5:13 p.m. ET
Apple ’s ( AAPL ) recently increased share repurchase plan is more than just retiring a lot of stock. It may also be a significant component of the daily volume in the stock’s buying and selling. And that could provide a "floor" for the stock—a support for the share price. Illustration: Adam Berry/Getty Images for Apple
That's one takeaway from a report today by Toni Sacconaghi of Bernstein . Sacconaghi, who rates Apple stock Market Perform, notes that the company’s share buybacks in the first quarter were about 6% of its daily trading volume. Combine that with purchases by Warren Buffett , chairman and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKA ), who has been gushing over the stock , and the combined purchases made up about 9% of Apple’s daily trading volume.
With Apple having announced a new buyback authorization of $100 billion over an unspecified time period, Sacconaghi thinks the Apple purchases, and what he presumes will be continued buying by Buffett, will continue to constitute a high percentage of daily volume next year to year and a half:
We note that Apple repurchased 6% of its shares traded in CY Q1; along with Warren Buffett's share purchases, the two accounted for over 9% of shares traded in CQ1, putting a strong "buy bid" under the stock, and likely tempering investor skittishness. Looking forward, we believe Apple could repurchase 4% - 8% of its share volume per quarter over the next 4 - 6 quarters; Buffett's recent rhetoric suggests he could also add to his already large position.
Looking back to when Buffett was buying shares of IBM ( IBM )—a stock he said Berkshire has now gotten out of—the Buffett buying could be a support for Apple shares, he muses:
It is difficult to determine whether — and at what level — aggressive share repurchases can help "support" a stock. Our analysis reveals that historically, there is little quarterly correlation between share repurchase levels and stock performance. That said, there are few meaningful precedents where share repurchases have amounted to 5%-10% of shares traded in a given quarter. One potentially useful analogy is IBM in 2011, when the combination of IBM + Warren Buffett amounted to more than 10% of share volumes, and IBM's stock outperformed materially in both quarters. Moreover, with Buffett exiting his IBM position over the last several quarters, the stock has fared poorly. That said, we note that there are other relatively high share repurchase quarters where IBM's stock did not outperform (though — arguably — the repurchases could have mitigated what would have been more notable underperformance in the shares).
Apple stock today closed up 89 cents, half a percent, at $186.05.
